title: Calculation rule
purpose: Add or edit the calculation and the laboratory's rounding for the manual results of one exact test, so analysts enter readings and the application works the result.
summary: Make manual results of one test calculated from readings, and set how the calculated value is rounded. Only administrators can save; other staff read these rules on QC configuration.

tasks.title: Add a calculation rule for a test
steps: Choose the [[Test]] and the [[Calculation]]. Choose the rounding in [[Round to]] and [[Digits]], and the rule for [[When the dropped digits are exactly 5]].
Record the method or SOP in [[Basis]].
Select [[Add calculation rule]]. From then on, analysts enter readings for that test.

tasks.title: Round larger values differently
steps: Enter the size in [[Second rounding from]], in the unit of the test.
Choose [[Round larger values to]] and [[Digits for larger values]], then save. Calculated values at or above that size use them.

tasks.title: Change a rule
steps: Open it from QC configuration and change the values.
Explain why in [[Reason for change]] and select [[Save changes]].

tasks.title: Go back to typed results for a test
steps: Clear [[Active]], give a reason and select [[Save changes]]. The rule and the worksheets already recorded stay.

good_to_know: There is no default rounding. Your rule rounds a calculated value once, at the end, and the reporting limit a preparation calculation works out. Typed and imported results are never rounded.
Changing or deactivating a rule never touches worksheets already recorded. Each keeps the rounding it was worked with.
A rule applies to manual entry only. File imports still supply final values and get no worksheet.
A calculation can only be chosen for a test whose unit it gives, and a dry-weight calculation only for a soil test. Units are not converted.
If you add or deactivate a rule, or choose another calculation, a page an analyst already had open is refused on save. A new rounding simply applies from the next save.

sections.title: Create, edit and access
paragraphs: Only administrators can open and save this form; other staff read these rules on the QC configuration page, where the rows are not links for them. Add creates a new configuration record; Edit prepopulates the existing record and requires a Reason for change. These are laboratory policy values: nothing here supplies a default rounding, and synthetic seed data is not a validated set.

items.label: Test
items.description: Required. One exact test: method version, analyte and matrix, listed by method, analyte and matrix. Manual results of that test are then worked from readings and a typed final result is refused. Only one rule can exist for a test, active or not; edit the existing one.

items.label: Calculation
items.description: Required. Reading times dilution factor, Solids by weight (balance in grams or milligrams), Preparation by volume, Prepared solid as weighed, Prepared solid corrected to dry weight (each of the last two in three unit pairings), Percent solids by weight or Percent moisture by weight. New entries use the current version; each result keeps the version it was worked with. A calculation that gives one unit is refused for a test whose unit differs, and a dry-weight calculation is refused for a test whose matrix is not soil. Units are not converted; only the spelling of micro may differ (µ, μ or u). Reading times dilution factor and Preparation by volume work for a test in any unit, but Preparation by volume takes a volume of sample and is refused for a soil test. A rule that names a calculation this release no longer has is shown as not in this release and must be changed.

items.label: Round to
items.description: Required. Significant figures or Decimal places. This is the laboratory's own choice. It rounds the calculated value and also a reporting limit the calculation works out (the preparation calculations).

items.label: Digits
items.description: Required whole number. 1 to 15 for significant figures; 0 to 10 for decimal places (0 rounds to whole numbers). Results are stored to 10 decimal places: a rounding that would need more for a value, for example many significant figures of a value below 1, is refused when that value is entered.

items.label: Second rounding from
items.description: Optional size in the unit of the test (up to 10 decimal places), greater than zero. A calculated value whose size before rounding is at or above it uses the second rounding below; smaller values use Round to and Digits. Because the choice is made before rounding, a value just under this size can round up to it and still show the digits of the smaller range. Blank means one rounding for every value. Giving it requires the two fields below, and they cannot be given without it.

items.label: Round larger values to
items.description: Significant figures or Decimal places for values at or above Second rounding from.

items.label: Digits for larger values
items.description: Digits for those larger values, with the same limits as Digits.

items.label: When the dropped digits are exactly 5
items.description: Required. Half to even (a final 5 rounds to the nearest even digit) or Half up (a final 5 always rounds away from zero). The value is carried at full precision and rounded once, at the end.

items.label: Basis
items.description: Required, not blank. The method or SOP the calculation and rounding come from. It is copied onto each worksheet as the basis of the rule.

items.label: Active
items.description: Initially checked on Add. Only an active rule changes how the test is entered. Clearing it makes the test take typed results again; the rule and earlier worksheets stay.

items.label: Reading times dilution factor
items.description: The analyst enters the Instrument reading (a number, or ND) and the Reporting limit before dilution, offered from the test's catalog limit. Result = reading × dilution factor; reporting limit applied = limit before dilution × dilution factor. A reading of ND gives ND at that limit. Works for a test in any unit.

items.label: Solids by weight, balance in grams
items.description: Readings: Dried residue with its filter or dish (g), Filter or dish alone (g) and Sample volume (mL). Result in mg/L = (dried residue with its filter or dish − filter or dish alone) × 1,000,000 ÷ sample volume in mL.

items.label: Solids by weight, balance in milligrams
items.description: The same readings with the weights in mg. Result in mg/L = (dried residue with its filter or dish − filter or dish alone) × 1,000 ÷ sample volume in mL.

items.label: Preparation by volume
items.description: Readings: Instrument reading (a number, or ND), Reporting limit in the solution, Sample volume prepared (mL) and Final volume (mL). Result = instrument reading × final volume ÷ sample volume prepared × dilution factor. Works for a test in any unit that is not a soil test.

items.label: Prepared solid as weighed
items.description: Three pairings of the unit read in the solution to the unit of the result: mg/L to mg/kg, ug/L to ug/kg, ug/L to mg/kg. Readings: Instrument reading (or ND), Reporting limit in the solution, Final volume (mL) and Sample weight (g). Result = instrument reading × final volume in mL ÷ sample weight in g × dilution factor, divided by 1,000 again for ug/L to mg/kg. No percent solids correction: the result is on the basis of the portion as weighed, and the analyst declares wet or dry weight.

items.label: Prepared solid corrected to dry weight
items.description: The same three pairings and readings, with Sample weight as received (g). The result is the same arithmetic divided by percent solids ÷ 100. Soil tests only. The analyst must declare Dry weight, which the entry offers. Percent solids and its source reference are required: the percent solids comes from the entry's Percent solids field, is not typed a second time as a reading and is kept on the worksheet as a reading.

items.label: Percent solids by weight, Percent moisture by weight
items.description: Three weights in g: Dish alone, Dish with the sample as received and Dish with the dried sample. Percent solids = (dish with the dried sample − dish alone) ÷ (dish with the sample as received − dish alone) × 100. Percent moisture = (dish with the sample as received − dish with the dried sample) ÷ (dish with the sample as received − dish alone) × 100. Results in %, so the test's unit must be %. Weights in which the dried sample is lighter than the dish, or heavier than the sample as received, are refused at entry. On a soil entry the analyst must declare Wet weight, which the entry offers. The reporting limit is typed, and no dilution factor is applied.

items.label: What the solids, percent solids and percent moisture calculations do not do
items.description: They apply no dilution factor (it must be 1). Solids by weight also applies no blank correction. The reporting limit applied is still typed by the analyst. The source named on each worksheet gives the reference the formula comes from.

items.label: What the preparation calculations work out
items.description: Preparation by volume and the prepared solid calculations work out the reporting limit applied: the reporting limit in the solution times the same factors as the result, then rounded by this rule, the same rule as the result. A reading of ND gives ND at that limit. The worksheet keeps the limit before rounding, and Worked again now checks the limit too. A rounding that takes the limit to zero is refused when the result is entered. The percent solids for a dry-weight correction is typed with its source and is not taken from the sample's percent solids result. Volumes and weights are typed with each result and are not recorded once on a prepared aliquot.

sections.title: Rules and effects
paragraphs: With an active rule, manual entry of the test on the batch entry grid and on the result page takes the readings instead of a final result, and a typed final result is refused. The value is worked at full precision and rounded once by this rule. On a soil test, a calculation that means one weight basis (Dry weight, or Wet weight for percent solids and percent moisture) is refused with any other basis. A calculated value below the reporting limit applied needs a qualifier, or the analyst ticks Report as ND (allowed only below the limit).

File imports are unchanged: they supply final values kept with their source, get no worksheet and are not recalculated. QC sample measurements are still typed. Typed and imported values are never rounded.

Each calculated revision keeps a worksheet with the readings, the unrounded value, the unrounded reporting limit where the calculation works it out, the rounding applied and this rule's basis. A later change to the rule does not touch earlier worksheets, and a correction adds a new revision with its own worksheet.

The rule is read again when the analyst saves. If a rule was added or deactivated, or its calculation replaced, after the analyst opened the entry grid or the result page, saving is refused with the reason and the analyst reloads: readings typed for one calculation are never worked with another. A change to the rounding alone is not a refusal; it applies from the next save. If the test's unit later stops matching the calculation, a dry-weight calculation stands on a test that is not soil, or this release no longer has the calculation, entry is refused and says an administrator must correct the rule.

items.label: Add calculation rule
items.description: Validate and create the rule, then return to QC configuration.

sections.title: Save, cancel and history
paragraphs: Validation errors appear beside their fields and preserve entered values. A stale form is refused rather than overwriting another person's edit; input stays visible, but reload and compare current values before saving again.

items.label: Reason for change
items.description: Optional on creation; required nonblank for every existing-row save. Recorded with actor, time and before and after values.

items.label: Save changes
items.description: For an edit, validate the fields, recheck that the record still matches the version opened, and save with its audit event. Success returns to QC configuration.

items.label: Cancel
items.description: Return to QC configuration without saving typed changes.

items.label: History
items.description: Existing rules show their latest 20 audit events, displayed oldest to newest, with action, actor, time and reason. No history section appears before any events exist.
